package_info.why_malicious: This article is an industry overview and does not describe a specific malicious package or code. It discusses the growing risk of software supply chain attacks, referencing incidents like SolarWinds and CodeCov, and highlights the lack of detection and monitoring tools in most organizations. No specific malicious package or code is analyzed.

behavioral_signatures: Software tampering at any phase of the SDLC
Unauthorized modification of release packages or CI/CD artifacts
Unexpected changes in container images or build outputs
file_indicators: Modified or injected files in release packages
network_indicators: Unusual outbound connections from build or CI/CD environments
Connections to known malicious infrastructure during build or release
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Implement automated monitoring and integrity checks at every phase of the software development lifecycle (SDLC), including CI/CD pipelines, container builds, and release packaging. Use tools that can detect unauthorized changes, malware, backdoors, and exposed secrets in software artifacts before public distribution. Monitor for unexpected network activity from build environments and validate the integrity of all third-party and open-source dependencies.
